items.title: The number of isolated vertices at the two ends of the window: at least one and at most d below, none above
items.author: Sahar Diskin, Anna Geisler
items.work: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement pins down the number of isolated vertices at the two ends of the window (author lemma at source lines 608-615, label lem:number-isolates): at least one and at most d at the lower end, and none at the upper end, each with high probability. The proof (source lines 617-635) combines two first-moment estimates of the expectation n(1-p)^d with a second-moment computation that distinguishes non-adjacent from adjacent pairs of vertices, using the edge count nd/2 of the product graph (proof lines 626-633), and closes with Chebyshev's inequality. The pair counting is the part with content. H2.
